why: the work is read-only research that has to end in a phased platform plan, and no single playbook covers both
result: worked, the phase structure came from multi-phase-plan and the verification gates from figure-it-out

why: four repos and roughly a hundred plan files would have eaten the context window before any writing started
result: explorers had not returned by the time the docs were written, so the parent read the binding plan files directly instead

decision: read the Omnigent README, the Databricks blog, and the Databricks docs page myself, and sent a fourth agent to mine the rest
why: the architecture claims are the load-bearing citations, so the parent should read the primary sources first hand
result: three abstractions kept: narrow host adapter, declared capability matrix, bench that fails closed

decision: fetched raw markdown from GitHub after the docs site returned SPA shell instead of content
why: WebFetch against the hosted docs returned Next.js scaffolding with no prose
result: worked, raw markdown had the full architecture text

decision: read 00-vision, 01-architecture, 06-platform-config, TASK-GRAPH, DRV-KERNEL, DRV-EVENTS in the main thread
why: the crux question is whether drivecode-sdk collides with the already-planned @cline/drive kernel, and that cannot be answered from a summary
result: found the collision, D1 already specifies a pure kernel at sdk/packages/drive

decision: ran a three-candidate design arena on the layer boundary instead of deciding solo
why: merge versus separate package is close to a one-way door, it sets the package graph every later feature is written against
result: two candidates said merge, one said sits above

decision: chose merge, drivecode-sdk is @cline/drive with a host port added
why: the dissent argued a host port violates D1 purity, but DriveHostPort is an interface with no implementation and declaring an effect is not performing one
result: adopted, and the dissent's own MVP surface re-exports six kernel functions, which is a pass-through package

decision: monorepo, not a separate drivecode-sdk repository
why: cursor-drive and claude-drive both carry a hand-maintained syncTypes.ts and both AGENTS.md tell a human to sync manually, which is the failure mode to design out
result: adopted, publishing is the cross-repo boundary and copy-paste is not

decision: kept the Drive schemas in @cline/shared rather than moving them into the harness
why: a non-Cline host would have to pull the hook engine and extension registry to get a DriveEvent type, which is the wrong shape, but that cost is only paid when a second host exists and the move is a mechanical refactor with a compiler behind it
result: deferred with an escape hatch, drive imports from shared are type-only so extraction is a file move

decision: split the 01-architecture package map row that assigns room, roster, and stage ops to @cline/core
why: the pure fold and the single-writer commit are different things, and leaving the fold in core means the webview cannot import it and will grow a second reducer
result: adopted, reduceRoom and projectStage move to @cline/drive, commitRoomOp and broadcast stay in core

decision: capability descriptor uses Drive-feature flags plus harnessId, schemaVersion, and a required writerEndpoint
why: callers branch on Drive features not harness internals, and making the writer endpoint required means a host cannot forget to declare who the single writer is
result: adopted, a host declaring 7891 is now visible in a diff and in a bench report

decision: conformance kit must fail closed, tested with a host that declares a capability and no-ops
why: a kit that only ever passes is decoration, the Omnigent lesson is that the matrix rots into marketing without a bench behind it

decision: riskiest unknown first, fakeHost in Phase 2 before any hub code exists
why: the real risk is that the port is too Cline-shaped for a second host, and writing the Cline binding first would bias the port toward whatever the hub happens to expose
result: adopted, Phase 5 criterion 1 is the honest test and Phase 2 fakeHost is the proxy

decision: recorded that Phases 1 and 2 have static verification only
why: there is no runtime surface until Phase 3, so control-cli and control-ui cannot apply, and pretending otherwise would hide where the first real evidence arrives

decision: folded the arena cross-judge into a background run rather than blocking on it
why: the parent had already read all three candidates and the dissent's central argument is refutable on a point of fact, so the judge is a check rather than a tiebreak
